name: Plate-Loaded Machine Row — High Row
description: The plate-loaded high row machine (such as the Hammer Strength High Row) features independent arms that allow each side to move through a natural arc, accommodating individual shoulder mechanics. The high row angle targets the upper lats, rhomboids, and rear deltoids more directly than a low or neutral row. The chest is supported, eliminating lower back involvement and allowing isolation of the upper back musculature.

execution.starting_position: Load the machine with weight plates. Sit facing the machine with the chest on the pad. Grip the handles at a neutral or pronated position with arms extended.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust seat height so the handles are level with the upper chest or face when seated. Keep the chest on the pad throughout the movement.
steps: Step 1: Grip the handles with the arms extended, chest on the pad.
Step 2: Retract the scapulae and pull both handles toward the upper chest/face.
Step 3: Drive the elbows back and out, keeping them at approximately shoulder height.
Step 4: Squeeze hard at peak contraction.
Step 5: Return under control to full extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Pulling the handles too low, shifting from a high row to a mid row pattern
Not fully extending at the bottom of each rep
safety_considerations: Adjust seat height carefully — improper positioning causes shoulder impingement
Do not use excessive weight that prevents full scapular retraction
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension at the start to handles near the upper chest at the finish.
coaching_cues: Think rear delt and rhomboids — not just lats
